original_value: Crop-type identification is very important in agricultural regions. Most researchers in this area have focused on exploring the ability of synthetic-aperture radar (SAR) sensors to identify crops. This paper uses multi-source (Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2, and Landsat-8) and multi-temporal data to identify crop types. The change detection method was used to analyze spectral and indices information in time series. Significant differences in crop growth status during the growing season were found. Then, three obviously differentiated time features were extracted. Three advanced machine learning algorithms (Support Vector Machine, Artificial Neural Network, and Random Forest, RF) were used to identify the crop types. The results showed that the detection of (Vertical-vertical) VV, (Vertical-horizontal) VH, and Cross Ratio (CR) changes was effective for identifying land cover. Moreover, the red-edge changes were obviously different according to crop growth periods. Sentinel-2 and Landsat-8 showed different normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) changes also. By using single remote sensing data to classify crops, Sentinel-2 produced the highest overall accuracy (0.91) and Kappa coefficient (0.89). The combination of Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2, and Landsat-8 data provided the best overall accuracy (0.93) and Kappa coefficient (0.91). The RF method had the best performance in terms of identity classification. In addition, the indices feature dominated the classification results. The combination of phenological period information with multi-source remote sensing data can be used to explore a crop area and its status in the growing season. The results of crop classification can be used to analyze the density and distribution of crops. This study can also allow to determine crop growth status, improve crop yield estimation accuracy, and provide a basis for crop management.

result.paraphrase: Crop-type identification is crucial in agricultural regions. In this area, most researchers have concentrated on using synthetic-aperture radar (SAR) sensors to recognize crops. This paper applies multi-source data (Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2, and Landsat-8) together with multi-temporal observations to classify crop types. A change-detection approach was used to examine spectral and index information across time series, revealing marked differences in crop growth conditions during the growing season. Based on this, three clearly distinct temporal features were extracted. Three advanced machine-learning algorithms—Support Vector Machine, Artificial Neural Network, and Random Forest (RF)—were then employed for crop-type identification. The results indicated that tracking changes in VV (Vertical-vertical), VH (Vertical-horizontal), and Cross Ratio (CR) was effective for land-cover identification. Red-edge variations also differed noticeably across crop growth stages, and Sentinel-2 and Landsat-8 showed different NDVI change patterns. When classifying crops using single remote-sensing data, Sentinel-2 achieved the highest overall accuracy (0.91) and Kappa coefficient (0.89). The fusion of Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2, and Landsat-8 produced the best overall accuracy (0.93) and Kappa coefficient (0.91). RF delivered the best identification-classification performance, and index features played the dominant role in the classification results. Combining phenological-period information with multi-source remote-sensing data can be used to investigate crop area and growing-season status. Crop-classification results can help analyze crop density and distribution, assess crop growth status, improve yield-estimation accuracy, and provide a basis for crop management.
